operations.description: This API is used to add a file system to an AD domain. Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) is a directory service that provides unified identity and permissions management through domain networks. By adding an SFS Turbo file system to an AD domain, you can easily authenticate and manage user identities and control file permissions in that domain.

This API is used to batch add tags for a specified file system. A maximum of 20 tags can be added to a file system. Tag keys added to the same file system must be unique. This API is idempotent. If the file system already has the key you want to add, the tag will be updated.

This API is used to change the security group associated with an SFS Turbo file system. Security group change is an asynchronous task. You can check whether the security group is changed based on the value of **sub_status** returned after calling the API to query details of a file system. If value **232** is returned, the security group has been changed.
This API is used to change the name of an SFS Turbo file system.
This API is used to add a storage backend for an SFS Turbo file system.
This API is used to create a directory.
This API is used to create quotas for a directory.

This API is used to create an asynchronous task for a file system. Only tasks for querying directory usage can be created. Such tasks are also referred to as DU tasks. The value of **feature** in the API request path is **dir-usage**.
This API is used to create an import or export task.
This API is used to bind to an LDAP server.
This API is used to create a permission rule.
This API is used to create a file system.

This API is used to add a tag to a specified file system. A maximum of 20 tags can be added to a file system. Tag keys added to the same file system must be unique. This API is idempotent. If the file system already has the key you want to add, the tag will be updated.

This API is used to remove a file system from an AD domain. AD DS is a directory service that provides unified identity and permissions management through domain networks. By adding an SFS Turbo file system to an AD domain, you can easily authenticate and manage user identities and control file permissions in that domain.
This API is used to delete a backend target.
This API is used to delete a directory.
This API is used to delete quotas of a directory.

If the asynchronous task is being executed, this API is used to cancel and then delete the task. Otherwise, this API is used to delete the task. Only tasks for querying directory usage can be deleted. Such tasks are also referred to as DU tasks. The value of **feature** in the API request path is **dir-usage**.
This API is used to delete an import or export task.
This API is used to delete the LDAP configuration.
This API is used to delete a permission rule.
This API is used to delete a file system.
This API is used to delete a tag of a specified file system. If the key to be deleted does not exist, error 404 will be returned.
This API is used to expand the capacity of a file system.
This API is used to query backend targets of a file system.

This API is used to obtain the asynchronous tasks of a file system. Only tasks for querying directory usage can be obtained. Such tasks are also referred to as DU tasks. The value of **feature** in the API request path is **dir-usage**.
This API is used to list import and export tasks.
This API is used to query the permission rules of a file system.
This API is used to query the tags of all file systems of a tenant.
This API is used to obtain the file system list.
Querying the File System List by Tag

This API is used to query the AD domain configuration. AD DS is a directory service that provides unified identity and permissions management through domain networks. By adding an SFS Turbo file system to an AD domain, you can easily authenticate and manage user identities and control file permissions in that domain.
This API is used to obtain details about a backend target.
This API is used to obtain the IP addresses of the clients who have mounted the file system.
This API is used to query whether a directory exists.
This API is used to update quotas of a directory. The **used_capacity** and **used_inode** obtained may not be the latest.

This API is used to query the usage of a file system directory (including usages of subdirectories). The obtained data may not be the latest as there is a 5-minute delay between the frontend and backend.

This API is used to obtain details about a file system asynchronous task. Only tasks for querying directory usage can be obtained. Such tasks are also referred to as DU tasks. The value of **feature** in the API request path is **dir-usage**.
This API is used to query details about an import or export task.

This API is used to query the execution status of an SFS Turbo asynchronous task. For example, you can query the task execution status using the **jobId** returned after you call the API for creating and binding the LDAP configuration.
This API is used to query the LDAP configuration.
This API is used to query a specific permission rule of a file system.
Querying tenant quotas
This API is used to query details about an SFS Turbo file system.
This API is used to query all tags of a specified file system.

This API is used to modify the AD domain configuration. AD DS is a directory service that provides unified identity and permissions management through domain networks. By adding an SFS Turbo file system to an AD domain, you can easily authenticate and manage user identities and control file permissions in that domain.
This API is used to update quotas of a directory.
This API is used to update the cold data eviction period of a file system.
This API is used to modify the LDAP configuration.
This API is used to update the properties of a storage backend.
This API is used to update the auto synchronization policy of a storage backend.
This API is used to modify a permission rule.
